A simulation ensemble as a mechanism lens

Source: R/lens_builtin.R
lens_mechanism.Rd

Reads a simulation ensemble as a lens on the response over a candidate grid: one row of the ensemble's outputs per ensemble member, one column per grid point. The simulator is the most independent witness the orchestra has – it shares no sampler, no objective, no priors and no data preparation with any statistical lens – and it is the only lens that can express a plateau, a threshold or a non-monotone response without being told to look for one, so it declares all four shapes.

Usage

lens_mechanism(ensemble, grid, output = NULL, name = "mechanism")

Arguments

ensemble

A simulation ensemble: an fb_ensemble(), a PESTO calibration manifest, a saved .rds path, or a list carrying params and outputs. It reaches the canonical shape through as_fb_ensemble(), so an object no coercer covers is a programmer error rather than a decline.

grid

Non-empty numeric vector of candidate values the response is read over.

output

Which output columns carry the response, when the ensemble holds more than one output set: a character vector of column names, or a single string naming a value of the ensemble's output_dims$variable. NULL (the default) takes every output column, which is right for a single-output ensemble.

name

Single non-empty string naming the lens.

Value

A quorum_lens() of kind response_curve whose fit() returns a quorum_draws() matrix with one row per ensemble member and one column per grid point, or a quorum_abstention() with reason grid_mismatch (the selected outputs do not cover the grid) or outputs_not_numeric (the selected columns do not hold a numeric response).

Details

quorum never runs the simulator. The ensemble is produced upstream and reaches this function through the C5 ingest contract, so a pesto_ensemble_manifest, a saved ensemble and a bare list carrying params and outputs are all accepted on the same terms.

The grid check is the substance of this adapter. An ensemble whose outputs do not cover the grid – the wrong number of columns, or numerically-named columns naming different values from the grid – is a mismatch between two descriptions of the same axis, and reading it anyway would silently attach the simulator's response to the wrong candidates. It returns a typed grid_mismatch decline instead.

See also

fb_ensemble() and as_fb_ensemble() for the ingest contract.

Examples

ens <- fb_ensemble(
  params = data.frame(k = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)),
  outputs = data.frame(a = c(4.1, 4.6, 5.0), b = c(5.2, 5.9, 6.1))
)
l <- lens_mechanism(ens, grid = c(0, 50))
dim(S7::prop(S7::prop(l, "fit")(NULL, NULL), "draws"))
#> [1] 3 2

# A grid the outputs do not cover is declined, not stretched to fit.
is_quorum_abstention(lens_mechanism(ens, grid = c(0, 50, 100)))
#> [1] TRUE
